# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Iteration 1/3. Parent = seed (val 0.148: 0 solid / 2 flaky / 7 failing / 1 infra). Prompt-only capability.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | pandas whole-sheet round-trip corrupts the file | 168-17, 188-39, 52532, 53449, 438-18(flaky) | `df.to_excel` drops other sheets, adds a header row that shifts data down, appends a NEW column instead of the target column, and parses text→datetime/number. Scorer checks cells by coordinate + all-other-cells-unchanged, so every one of these mutations mismatches. | CAPABILITY-GAP (method) | worked method: openpyxl in-place edit; contract: preserve untouched cells/types |
| 2 | hardcoded / non-generalizing answer | 43213, 47766, 52532, 53449 | Agent writes a value eyeballed from the preview (43213 wrote literal `0.0`; 47766 hardcoded year `2023`), or computes only for copy 1. Final block is replayed on 3 different-data copies → the constant is wrong for the other two → 0/3. | KNOWLEDGE | contract: compute each answer cell from the data the code reads, never hardcode |
| 3 | writes to guessed coordinates / never inspects | 43213, 52532, 188-39, 53449, 56915 | Agent skips to a solution using assumed pandas column names (KeyError → 188-39 wrote no file) or assumed cell positions / data extent ("check where the data actually ends" — 56915). Template's step-1 inspect was optional ("e.g."). | BEHAVIORAL (skipped step) | ordered procedure: INSPECT as an unavoidable first step; locate table dynamically |
| 4 | verification skipped → stops on unverified output | all failing + both flaky | Template said "verify" but agents re-paste the solution code and then stop; no turn actually re-opens output and checks values. | BEHAVIORAL (skipped step) | pre-finish checklist as a precondition of replying with no code block |
| 5 | wrong value TYPE in written cells | 43213 (int vs float), 56915 (str/#N/A vs float), 438-18 (datetime vs str) | Written cells have the wrong type; pandas parsing also flips text→date. | CONTRACT | explicit type rule (number as number, float where fractional, text stays text) |
| 6 | first turn wasted on `<think>` with no code block | 160-6, 47766, 52532, 53449 (t0s) | Reader (Qwen3-8B) emits a reasoning-only reply, no ```python block → round wasted, fewer turns left to verify → flakiness. | BEHAVIORAL | rule: every reply is exactly one code block, reasoning as `#` comments |
| — | ENV / infra fault (handed back, NOT edited) | 49945 (all 3 trials), plus scattered single-trial timeouts on 47766/52532 | `sandbox exec failed: HTTPConnectionPool(127.0.0.1) Read timed out (180s)`. Container/network noise, not a prompt defect. | — | none — diagnosis only |

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit)
| cluster | edit class | file | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | worked method + contract | prompt.md | Mandate openpyxl `load_workbook` → write target cells by coordinate → `save`; forbid `df.to_excel` for writing (drops sheets/shifts rows/appends cols/reparses types). General idiom, no task specifics. | Flaky 160-6/438-18 are single/two-sheet tasks; in-place edit preserves them better than the current pandas rewrite (438-18's flaky failure WAS pandas datetime reparse). No solid task to regress. |
| 2 | contract (rewrote the old "prefer literals" line) | prompt.md | "Compute each answer cell from the data the code reads; never hardcode a preview value" + 3-copy-replay rationale. Kept LITERAL output (NOT formulas — see below). | Delete-row flaky tasks write no derived values → unaffected. |
| 3 | ordered procedure (precondition) | task_template.md | Step 1 INSPECT is now mandatory and first: print sheet names, headers, column letters, and where data starts/ends before solving. | Additive; makes flaky tasks more robust, changes no correct behavior. |
| 4 | pre-finish checklist (precondition) | task_template.md | May reply without code ONLY after re-opening output_path and confirming value + type + nothing-outside-range-changed + sheets-present. | Additive; can only raise consistency on flaky tasks. |
| 5 | type contract | prompt.md | number-as-number, float where fractional, text stays text, no new/renamed columns, don't write past the answer's last row, guard `None` source cells. | Additive constraint; passing tasks already satisfy it. |
| 6 | working rule | prompt.md + task_template.md | Every reply = exactly one ```python block, reasoning as `#` comments. | Additive; reduces wasted rounds → helps flaky consistency. |

## Verify-the-fix (trace → what the edit changes on those exact inputs)
- 188-39 trace: `df_result` read with pandas → `KeyError 'Location'` → no output file. openpyxl-in-place + mandatory INSPECT means it reads the real column letters and writes cells directly; no KeyError, output is written. Fixes the "produced NO output" 0.
- 168-17 trace: `df.to_excel(index=False)` wrote a header row + shifted data into A2:E12 where the gold expects those cells empty ("written past where the answer ends; changed original input"). In-place `delete_rows` leaves untouched cells untouched. Directly addresses the mismatch class.
- 43213 trace: wrote literal `0.0` to B12:B15 (guessed) and int not float. Edit 2 (compute from data) + Edit 5 (float) → code reads B11.. and computes the running averages as floats → generalizes to all 3 copies. Feedback was exactly "int where float expected" + "LOWER than expected".
- 52532 trace: `to_excel` appended a new `H` column, leaving real H2:H8 unchanged ("UNCHANGED byte-identical", "empty where value expected"). openpyxl writes H2:H8 by coordinate; INSPECT fixes the header-offset guess. 
- 53449 / 56915 traces: category/lookup written to a new column or as #N/A strings ("written past where answer ends"; "str where float expected"). In-place coordinate writes + type rule + dynamic data-extent inspection target these mismatches.
- 438-18 (flaky) trace: pandas parsed text→datetime ("datetime where str was expected") and changed original cells. openpyxl in-place keeps original text/type → removes the failing trial's cause.
- 160-6 / 47766 t0: reasoning-only reply, round wasted. Edit 6 makes every reply carry a code block.

## Blast-radius statement
No SOLID passing tasks exist (0/10). The only tasks with reward>0 are flaky 160-6 and 438-18 (0.67, delete-rows / value-replace). Every edit is either ADDITIVE (3,4,5,6) or a method/contract change that does not flip behavior on those two (1,2 concern value-writing & derived-value generalization; the flaky tasks either restructure rows or copy existing text). Risk is bounded and asymmetric: 7 dead-zero tasks × 3 trials to gain vs 2 flaky tasks to protect.

## Value-vs-formula decision (IMPORTANT, recorded so it is not re-litigated)
Memory `libreoffice-recalc-active` proves recalc runs at GRADING time, so formulas CAN score. BUT the agent's own in-sandbox verification opens output with `data_only=True` and NO recalc, so a freshly-written formula reads back as `None`/formula-string — which would defeat the value+type verification checklist (Edit 4) and is an unbounded flip of the "prefer literals" rule that risks literal-passing tasks. So I deliberately kept the LITERAL path and made it generalize via "compute in code from the data read" rather than switching to live formulas. This is the safe lever the memory note recommends (dynamic table location + type preservation + guard missing source values), not the risky one.

## Process & features used
- Serial (single agent): read all trajectories directly via a small dump script; the cluster count was small enough that fan-out wasn't needed. Diagnosis grounded in the actual traces, not the summary.
- Prior iterations: none exist (iteration 1; RUNMAP/prior_iterations empty). Read LEDGER (baseline only), JOURNAL/INSIGHTS (empty), and the two memory notes (recalc-active, ground-truth-data).

## Good things to PRESERVE
- LITERAL output computed in code (do NOT switch to live formulas — breaks in-sandbox verification; see decision above).
- openpyxl in-place editing over pandas `to_excel` for writing.
- INSPECT-first and VERIFY-before-stop as unavoidable steps.

## Deliberately skipped
- 49945: infrastructure timeout on all trials — not a capability defect; no edit made on its account.
- 47766 / 56915 are hard reasoning/merged-cell lookups; I did not add task-specific logic (would overfit). The method + inspect + compute-from-data edits give them a better chance without hardcoding.
